output: The group of input objects is used to account for non-uniform room air temperatures that may occur within the interior air volume of a zone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, when was room air modeling added to the software?
output: Room air modeling was added to EnergyPlus starting with Version 1.2.

input: From EnergyPlus, which types of analyses might benefit from localized modeling of room air variations?
output: Comfort, indoor air quality, and other analyses might benefit from localized modeling of how room air varies across space.

input: In EnergyPlus, what specific aspect of room air is currently addressed in the modeling?
output: Only the temperature distribution of room air within the zone is currently addressed in EnergyPlus.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does the modeling of room air allow for calculations?
output: It allows surface heat transfer and air system heat balance calculations to be made taking into account natural thermal stratification of air and different types of intentional air distribution designs.

input: In EnergyPlus, what types of air distribution designs are mentioned as examples in the context of room air modeling?
output: Under-floor and side-wall displacement ventilation are mentioned as examples of intentional air distribution designs.

input: According to EnergyPlus, why does it not have completely general methods of modeling room air?
output: Such models, like RANS-CFD, are too computationally expensive to use with EnergyPlus for the foreseeable future.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the limitation of the models available for room airflow configurations?
output: The models that are available in EnergyPlus offer only limited modeling capabilities for select room airflow configurations.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the standard model for room air that has long been used in building energy simulation?
output: The complete mixing model for room air has long been the standard in building energy simulation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is currently lacking in the consensus regarding modeling non-uniform air temperatures in buildings?
output: There is not currently a consensus on how to best model non-uniform air temperatures in buildings.

input: In EnergyPlus, what responsibility does the user have regarding the application of room air models?
output: It is up to the user to have a good understanding of when, where, and how to apply the room air models available in EnergyPlus.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the section provide regarding the models available?
output: The rest of this section provides some guidance in the way of examples and further discussion of the models available in EnergyPlus.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the air model algorithm associated with the Mixing air model key?
output: The air model algorithm associated with the Mixing air model key is Well-Mixed.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the input objects required for the UserDefined air model?
output: The input objects required for the UserDefined air model are ‘Room­Air­Model­Type’, ‘Room­Air:­Temperature­Pattern:­User­Defined’, and ‘Room­Air:­Temperature­Pattern:***’.

input: In EnergyPlus, what algorithm is used for the One-Node Displacement Ventilation air model?
output: The algorithm used for the One-Node Displacement Ventilation air model is Mundt.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what input objects are required for the Three-Node Displacement Ventilation air model?
output: The input objects required for the Three-Node Displacement Ventilation air model are ‘Room­Air­Model­Type’ and ‘Room­Air­Settings:­Three­Node­Displacement­Ventilation’.

input: In EnergyPlus, which air model is applicable to interior zones served by a UFAD system?
output: The Under-Floor Air Distribution Interior air model is applicable to interior zones served by a UFAD system.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what input objects are associated with the Under-Floor Air Distribution Exterior air model?
output: The input objects associated with the Under-Floor Air Distribution Exterior air model are ‘Room­Air­Model­Type’ and ‘Room­Air­Settings:­Under­Floor­Air­Distribution­Exterior’.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the air model algorithm for the Cross-Ventilation air model?
output: The air model algorithm for the Cross-Ventilation air model is UCSD Cross Ventilation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what input objects are required for the Cross-Ventilation air model?
output: The input objects required for the Cross-Ventilation air model are ‘Room­Air­Model­Type’ and ‘Room­Air­Settings:­Cross­Ventilation’.

input: In EnergyPlus, what object is used to determine the available air model for a zone during simulation?
output: EnergyPlus uses the Room­Air­Model­Type object to determine which air model is available for use in a given zone during the simulation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if no Room­Air­Model­Type object is specified for a zone?
output: If no Room­Air­Model­Type object is specified, then EnergyPlus will run with the conventional, completely mixing air model for each zone or the whole building.

input: From EnergyPlus, how many Room­Air­Model­Type objects can be specified for each zone?
output: Currently, only a single Room­Air­Model­Type object can be specified for each zone.

input: In EnergyPlus, can the air model be switched during a simulation?
output: You cannot switch between models during a simulation in EnergyPlus.

input: According to EnergyPlus, which models switch from displacement to mixing ventilation under certain operating conditions?
output: The UCSD Displacement, Cross Ventilation, and UFAD models switch from displacement to mixing ventilation when the operating conditions do not give rise to unmixed flow.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the 'Name' field in the Room­Air­Model­Type object?
output: The 'Name' field is an alpha field that serves as the air model name selected by the user and is used as an identifier.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the 'Zone Name' field in the Room­Air­Model­Type object indicate?
output: The 'Zone Name' field indicates the unique name of a Zone object defined elsewhere in the input file.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the type of room air model applied to a zone?
output: The type of room air model selected will be applied to the zone indicated by the 'Zone Name' field in the Room­Air­Model­Type object.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the alpha field 'Room-Air Modeling Type' indicate?
output: The alpha field 'Room-Air Modeling Type' indicates the room-air model used for the specified zone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default room-air model if no Room­Air­Model­Type object is specified?
output: The default room-air model is the conventional complete-mixing air model.

input: In EnergyPlus, which keyword specifies the User Defined Room Air Temperature Patterns?
output: The keyword 'UserDefined' specifies the User Defined Room Air Temperature Patterns.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what air model is specified by the keyword 'OneNodeDisplacementVentilation'?
output: The keyword 'OneNodeDisplacementVentilation' specifies the Mundt one node displacement ventilation air model for displacement ventilation.

input: In EnergyPlus, which keyword specifies the three-node displacement ventilation model developed by the University of California, San Diego?
output: The keyword 'ThreeNodeDisplacementVentilation' specifies the three-node displacement ventilation model developed by the University of California, San Diego (UCSD DV).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what model is specified by the keyword 'CrossVentilation'?
output: The keyword 'CrossVentilation' specifies the two-zone cross ventilation model developed by the University of California, San Diego (UCSD CV).

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the keyword 'UnderFloorAirDistributionInterior' specify?
output: The keyword 'UnderFloorAirDistributionInterior' specifies the two-node interior zone under floor air distribution model developed by the University of California, San Diego (UCSD UFI).

input: According to EnergyPlus, which keyword specifies the two-node exterior zone under floor air distribution model?
output: The keyword 'UnderFloorAirDistributionExterior' specifies the two-node exterior zone under floor air distribution model developed by the University of California, San Diego (UCSD UFE).

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the alpha field 'Air Temperature Coupling Strategy' indicate?
output: This alpha field indicates how air temperatures predicted by the air models are used by the surface heat balance calculation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the two different coupling schemes available for air temperature coupling?
output: The two different coupling schemes available are Direct (also known as T-couple) and Indirect (DT-couple).

input: In EnergyPlus, when is indirect coupling more suited according to the air temperature coupling strategy?
output: Indirect coupling is more suited to situations where room air is well controlled and/or the room air model is less robust.

input: From EnergyPlus, when is direct coupling more appropriate for air temperature coupling?
output: Direct coupling is more suited for floating zone air temperatures and/or accurate room air models.

input: According to EnergyPlus, which models can use either the direct or indirect coupling scheme?
output: The Mundt model can use either coupling scheme.

input: In EnergyPlus, which models ignore the air temperature coupling strategy field and use direct coupling?
output: The UCSD DV, UCSD CV, UCSD UFI, and UCSD UFE models ignore this field and use direct coupling.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the expected input for the air temperature coupling strategy?
output: The expected input is either Direct or Indirect.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the example IDF entry for the Room-Air Model Type with the air temperature coupling strategy set to Direct?
output: The example IDF entry is: RoomAirModelType, MOD1, ZONE ONE, ThreeNodeDisplacementVentilation, Direct.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object?
output: The RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object is used to explicitly define temperature patterns that are to be applied to the mean air temperature within a thermal zone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, why is the Room Air modeling option made available?
output: This option is made available to model the consequences of air temperature variations during the design phase when little information is available about the specifics of the air distribution system or positioning of various loads.

input: From EnergyPlus, how can the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object be utilized during the design phase?
output: It can be used to evaluate the energy implications of different design targets for the temperature patterns.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object relate to annual energy use implications?
output: It provides a method of modeling the annual energy use implications for air temperature distributions determined using separate analyses or measurements.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how can the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object assist in understanding air distribution systems?
output: This option could be used to understand the annual energy implications of an air distribution system that has been previously analyzed using Computational Fluid Dynamics.

input: From EnergyPlus, how does the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object differ from other Room Air modeling approaches?
output: It differs in that the static temperature pattern is not really modeled, allowing it to respond to conditions that develop during the simulation.

input: In EnergyPlus, what factors can more sophisticated dynamic Room Air models adjust the temperature pattern based on?
output: Dynamic Room Air models will adjust the temperature pattern based on various factors such as air system flow rate, floor temperature, or rates of internal heat gains.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the role of the user-defined temperature distribution patterns in the simulation?
output: The user-defined temperature distribution patterns are fixed at the beginning, and EnergyPlus provides results that include the implications of those patterns.

input: In EnergyPlus, how can the user-defined temperature distribution option be useful for checking dynamic Room Air models?
output: It may be useful for checking dynamic Room Air models by using 'bounding' analysis.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what caution should users take when defining temperature distributions with the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object?
output: Users should be cautious as it would be very easy to define a pattern that is non-physical and will lead to erroneous results.

input: From EnergyPlus, how should user-defined temperature distributions be balanced to avoid violating energy conservation laws?
output: User-defined temperature distributions should probably be balanced about the mean to ensure that basic conservation of energy laws are not violated.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the 'Name' field in the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object?
output: The 'Name' field provides a unique name for this object.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the 'Zone Name' field represent in the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object?
output: The 'Zone Name' field provides the unique name of a zone described elsewhere in the file.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the 'Availability Schedule Name' field determine for the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined model?
output: The 'Availability Schedule Name' field provides the name of a schedule that will determine if this model is available.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens to the room air modeling when the availability schedule is not set for the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object?
output: When not available, the room air is modeled as completely mixed.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what values should the availability schedule be set to when the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined model is available or not?
output: The schedule should be set to '1.0' when the model is available and '0.0' when the model is not to be used.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the default value of the availability schedule if the field is left blank in the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined object?
output: If this field is blank, the schedule has values of 1 for all time periods.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Pattern Control Schedule Name field?
output: The Pattern Control Schedule Name field provides the name of the schedule that will be used to control which user-defined RoomAir temperature pattern will be applied at any given time.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what type of values must the schedule have that is linked to the RoomAir temperature patterns?
output: The schedule needs to have integer values that are closely coordinated with those defined as the second field in one of the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:* objects.

input: From EnergyPlus, how does the schedule affect the application of RoomAir temperature patterns during a simulation?
output: The schedule values provide the link to the actual patterns to be used throughout the day, allowing control over which user-defined pattern is used at different times during the simulation.

input: In EnergyPlus, how can a control schedule be utilized in relation to the air system's operation?
output: A control schedule could use one pattern when the air system is scheduled to be on, and a different pattern when the air system is scheduled to be off.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how can a control schedule respond to changing thermal loads throughout the day?
output: If the user has knowledge of how the air temperature pattern changes over the course of the day in response to changing thermal loads, then this schedule can be used to control when individual patterns are used.

input: From EnergyPlus, can you provide an example of how different patterns can be scheduled throughout the day?
output: A control schedule could use a pattern designated as number 100 from 18:00 to 6:00, pattern number 200 from 6:00 to 12:00, and pattern number 300 from 12:00 to 18:00.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is an example of a user-defined RoomAir temperature pattern object?
output: An example of this object is RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:UserDefined, Ground Floor South Air Temp Controls, ZN2_S_1, Always_on, Roomair Pattern 1.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:ConstantGradient object?
output: The RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:ConstantGradient object is used to model room air with a fixed temperature gradient in the vertical direction.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does the fixed-slope method in RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:ConstantGradient compare to other distribution patterns?
output: The fixed-slope method is about the simplest distribution pattern.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the three additional parameters included in the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:ConstantGradient that are important?
output: The three additional parameters are the temperature difference between the mean air temperature and the thermostat sensor location, the temperature difference between the mean air temperature and the point where system air is extracted, and the temperature difference affecting the air leaving the zone through exhaust fans.

input: According to EnergyPlus, why is the temperature difference between supply and return air significant?
output: The changes in temperature difference between supply and return can affect how an air system is controlled to meet the loads.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is an example of a source of input data for the vertical temperature gradient in the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:ConstantGradient?
output: An example of a source of input data for the vertical temperature gradient is ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 55-2004 Thermal Environmental Conditions for Human Occupancy.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does Table 5.2.4.3 in ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 55-2004 specify?
output: Table 5.2.4.3 specifies an allowable vertical temperature difference between head level and ankle level of 3ºC (5ºF).

input: In EnergyPlus, what temperature gradient results from a head to ankle length scale of 1.5 m (5 ft) and a vertical temperature difference of 3ºC?
output: This leads to a temperature gradient of 2.0 ºC/m.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the 'Name' field in the RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:ConstantGradient object?
output: The 'Name' field provides a unique name for this object.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what should the Control Integer for Pattern Control Schedule Name field contain?
output: This field should contain an integer value that is unique among all other RoomAir:TemperaturePattern:* objects.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Thermostat Offset field specify?
output: The Thermostat Offset field specifies the temperature difference between where the thermostat is situated and the mean air temperature.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is specified by the Return Air Offset field?
output: The Return Air Offset field specifies the temperature difference between the air leaving the zone and returning to the air system and the mean air temperature.

output: The RoomAir:Node object is used to define air nodes for a nodal air model.

output: The exact number of RoomAir:Node objects will vary based on the resolution of walls.

output: The minimum required types of RoomAir Nodes for the Mundt model are 'Inlet', 'Floor', 'Control', 'Ceiling', 'MundtRoom', and 'Return.'"

output: The alpha field 'Name' is a name for the air node that should be unique and is used as an identifier.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the alpha field 'Node Type' indicate about an air node?
output: The alpha field 'Node Type' indicates the type of the air node, with options available for use with the Mundt nodal air model.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the 'Inlet' specification refer to in the context of air nodes?
output: 'Inlet' is specified for the air node located where the system air enters the zone.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the 'Floor' specification indicate about the location of an air node?
output: 'Floor' is specified for the air node located near the floor.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the 'Control' specification refer to regarding air node placement?
output: 'Control' is specified for the air node located near the thermostat.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the 'Ceiling' specification indicate about an air node's location?
output: 'Ceiling' is specified for the air node located near the ceiling.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the 'MundtRoom' specification signify about an air node's position?
output: 'MundtRoom' is specified for the air node located adjacent to the wall(s).

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the 'Return' specification indicate about the air node's function?
output: 'Return' is specified for the air node located where the system air leaves the zone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the 'Zone Name' field represent for an air node?
output: 'Zone Name' indicates the name of the zone that this air node belongs to, which should be the unique name of a zone object defined elsewhere in the input file.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the significance of the 'Height of Nodal Control Volume Center' field?
output: The 'Height of Nodal Control Volume Center' indicates the height of the air node center, which is used by air models like the Mundt model to compute the air temperature as a function of height.

input: From EnergyPlus, how should the value for the 'Height of Nodal Control Volume Center' be specified?
output: The value for the 'Height of Nodal Control Volume Center' should be specified in meters and relative to the floor of the zone.

input: In EnergyPlus, what do the alpha fields in the Surface Name field indicate?
output: The alpha fields indicate the names of the surfaces that are interacting convectively with the air node.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how many surfaces are allowed to interact with a single air node?
output: Currently, at most 20 surfaces are allowed to interact with a single air node.

input: In EnergyPlus, when must surface names be specified for air nodes?
output: Surface names must be specified only for those nodes that interact with the inside faces of surfaces.

input: From EnergyPlus, how many nodes can a single surface couple to?

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the Fraction of Convective Internal Loads Added to Floor Air field represent?

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the Fraction of Infiltration Internal Loads Added to Floor Air field indicate?

input: In EnergyPlus, what type of air distribution system is the RoomAirSettings:ThreeNodeDisplacementVentilation model applicable to?
output: The model is applicable to spaces that are served by a low velocity floor-level displacement ventilation air distribution system.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the dominant sources of heat gain for the RoomAirSettings:ThreeNodeDisplacementVentilation model?
output: The dominant sources of heat gain should be from people and other localized sources located in the occupied part of the room.

input: From EnergyPlus, what caution should be taken when using the RoomAirSettings:ThreeNodeDisplacementVentilation model?

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the occupied subzone temperature (T$_\rmOC$) represent in the RoomAirSettings:ThreeNodeDisplacementVentilation model?
output: T$_\rmOC$ represents the temperature in the region between the floor layer and the upper, mixed layer.

input: From EnergyPlus, why is the upper node temperature (T$_\rmMX$) essential in the RoomAirSettings:ThreeNodeDisplacementVentilation model?
output: T$_\rmMX$ is essential for overall energy budget calculations and for modeling comfort effects of the upper layer temperature.

input: From EnergyPlus, what happens to the remainder of the convective portion of the internal gains in the occupied subzone?
output: The remainder of the convective portion of the internal gains in the occupied subzone enters the plumes and is carried to the upper subzone.

input: In EnergyPlus, what types of internal gains are assumed to be located in the occupied subzone?
output: The types of internal gains assumed to be located in the occupied subzone include people, task lights, electric equipment, gas equipment, hot water equipment, steam equipment, other equipment, and baseboard heat.

input: According to EnergyPlus, which types of internal gains are assumed to be in the upper subzone?
output: The types of internal gains assumed to be in the upper subzone include general lights, tubular daylighting devices, and high temperature radiant heaters.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the range of values for the schedule values in the 'Gain Distribution Schedule Name'?
output: The schedule values should be between 0 and 1.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does a schedule value of 1 signify for convective gains in the occupied subzone?
output: A schedule value of 1 means that all the convection gains from equipment, task lights, and people are dispersed in the lower occupied subzone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does a schedule value of 0 indicate regarding convective gains?
output: A schedule value of 0 puts all the lower subzone convective gains into the plumes rising into the upper well-mixed subzone.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the field 'Number of Plumes per Occupant' specify?
output: The field 'Number of Plumes per Occupant' specifies the number of plumes per occupant, which are associated with localized sources of convective heat gain from people and equipment.

input: From EnergyPlus, what value would be used for 'Number of Plumes per Occupant' if each occupant has a computer generating a separate plume?
output: A value of 2.0 would be used if each occupant has a computer that generates a separate plume that does not merge with the plume from the occupant in the lower, occupied, subzone.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the field 'Thermostat Height' represent?
output: The field 'Thermostat Height' represents the height in meters of the thermostat/temperature control sensor above the floor.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the 'Comfort Height' field used for?
output: The 'Comfort Height' field indicates the height in meters above the floor at which air temperature is calculated for comfort purposes.

output: The default value for 'Comfort Height' is 1.1 meters.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Temperature Difference Threshold for Reporting specify?
output: It specifies a minimum temperature difference between the upper mixed subzone and the occupied subzone that will be used to trigger whether or not the displacement ventilation auxiliary outputs will be calculated.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what auxiliary outputs are triggered by the Temperature Difference Threshold?
output: The auxiliary outputs include Room Air Zone Transition Height, Room Air Zone Recommended Minimum Flow Fraction, Room Air Zone Average Temperature Gradient, and Room Air Zone Maximum Temperature Gradient.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens to the outputs when the temperature difference is less than the threshold?
output: The outputs are set to negative values when the temperature difference is less than the threshold, and the output Room Air Zone Is Mixed Status is set to 1.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the unit of measurement for the Temperature Difference Threshold?
output: The value is in units of degrees Centigrade.

output: It represents the temperature of the upper well-mixed subzone in degrees C.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the Room Air Zone Occupied Subzone Temperature defined?
output: It is defined as the average temperature of the lower, stratified, occupied subzone in degrees C.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the Room Air Zone Floor Subzone Temperature indicate?
output: It indicates the temperature of the region near the floor in degrees C.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Room Air Zone Transition Height represent?
output: It represents the height above the floor, in meters, of the boundary between the lower occupied subzone and the upper well-mixed subzone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the Room Air Zone Recommended Minimum Flow Fraction?
output: It is the ratio of the minimum recommended flow rate to the actual flow rate, where flow rate means the sum of infiltration, ventilation, mixing, and system air flow rates.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Room Air Zone Is Mixed Status indicate?
output: It is an integer flag that indicates whether the zone is mixed (single node well-mixed zone model used) or stratified (UCSD DV model used), with 1 meaning well-mixed and 0 meaning stratified.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the Room Air Zone Average Temperature Gradient defined?
output: It is defined as the temperature gradient between the middle of the floor region and the middle of the well-mixed upper subzone in degrees Kelvin per meter.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the definition of the Room Air Zone Maximum Temperature Gradient?
output: The Room Air Zone Maximum Temperature Gradient is defined as the maximum of the temperature gradient between the middle of the floor region and the middle of the occupied subzone, and the temperature gradient between the middle of the occupied subzone and the middle of the well-mixed subzone, measured in degrees Kelvin per meter.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the Room Air Zone Thermal Comfort Effective Air Temperature specified?
output: The Room Air Zone Thermal Comfort Effective Air Temperature is specified at the user-defined comfort height in degrees Celsius.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the Room Air Zone Thermostat Temperature determined?
output: The Room Air Zone Thermostat Temperature is determined at the height of the thermostat, which is specified by user input, and is measured in degrees Celsius.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the UCSD Cross Ventilation Room Air Model provide?
output: The UCSD Cross Ventilation Room Air Model provides a simple model for heat transfer and temperature prediction in cross ventilated rooms.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is Cross Ventilation (CV) commonly found in?
output: Cross Ventilation (CV) is common in many naturally ventilated buildings.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does air flow in Cross Ventilation systems?
output: Air flows through windows, open doorways, and large internal apertures across rooms and corridors in the building.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the context in which the CV model is used?
output: The CV model is used in EnergyPlus in the context of natural ventilation simulations using the AirflowNetwork airflow prediction model.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the two clearly distinguishable flow regions in typical CV room flows?
output: The two clearly distinguishable flow regions are jet regions in front of the inflow windows and recirculation regions in the portions of the room that are not directly in front of the windows.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is each inflow aperture characterized in terms of airflow regions?
output: Each inflow aperture has one jet region while the recirculation regions are treated as a whole, with a single temperature and characteristic velocity.

input: In EnergyPlus, why is the default perfectly mixed single temperature node room air approach not suitable for CV flows?
output: The default EnergyPlus perfectly mixed single temperature node room air approach is not suitable for these partially mixed flows.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does the proposed CV model differ from the default approach?
output: The proposed CV model uses multiple nodes with distinct air temperature and airflow velocity, one node for the recirculations plus one additional node for each inflow aperture.

output: The 'Zone Name' field provides the name of the zone to which this object applies.

input: In EnergyPlus, how many instances of the ‘UCSD Cross Ventilation Model Controls’ object are needed for each zone modeled?
output: A single instance of the ‘UCSD Cross Ventilation Model Controls’ object is needed for each zone modeled using this method.

output: The 'Gain Distribution Schedule Name' field specifies the unique name of schedule defined elsewhere in the input file.

output: The schedule values define the fractions of the convective portion of the internal gains in the jet and recirculation regions.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what should the schedule values in the 'Gain Distribution Schedule Name' field be between?
output: The schedule values should be between 0 and 1.

output: A value of 1 means that all the convective gains are dispersed in the jet region.

output: A value of 0 puts all the convective gains into the recirculation region.

output: The 'Airflow Region Used for Thermal Comfort Evaluation' field is required whenever thermal comfort is predicted.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the 'Airflow Region Used for Thermal Comfort Evaluation' field define?
output: It defines air temperature and mean airflow velocity that will be used in the Fanger model.

input: In EnergyPlus, what conditions must the 'Airflow Region Used for Thermal Comfort Evaluation' field refer to?
output: Conditions must refer to one of the two regions defined in the model: jet or recirculation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the possible choices for the 'Airflow Region Used for Thermal Comfort Evaluation' field?
output: The possible choices are Jet or Recirculation.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the output for the average temperature in the jet region of the flow?
output: The output is the average air temperature in the jet region of the flow in degrees C, which is the inflow-area-weighted average if there is more than one inflow window.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the output for the average temperature in the recirculation region indicate?
output: The output indicates the average air temperature in the recirculation region of the flow in degrees C.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the average airflow velocity in the jet region of the flow defined?
output: The average airflow velocity in the jet region of the flow is defined in meters per second, and it is the inflow area weighted average of the jet inflow velocities if there is more than one inflow window.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the output for the average airflow velocity in front of the window represent?
output: The output represents the average airflow velocity in the jet region in front of the window, measured in meters per second.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the average airflow velocity in the recirculation region of the flow?
output: The average airflow velocity in the recirculation region of the flow is measured in meters per second.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the ratio between airflow rate in the recirculation regions and the total inflow rate defined?
output: The ratio is defined as non-dimensional and represents the airflow rate in the recirculation regions compared to the total inflow rate.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the significance of the inflow opening area output?
output: The inflow opening area output indicates the area of the inflow aperture in square meters, which can change due to variations in wind direction or opening schedules.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the room length output measure?
output: The room length output measures the length of the room along the cross ventilation direction in meters.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the integer flag for Is Mixing Status indicate?
output: The integer flag indicates whether the zone is mixed (with a value of 1 for well-mixed) or if significant momentum conservation is occurring (with a value of 0 for cross ventilation).

input: In EnergyPlus, what mechanisms can cause a transition to mixed flow in a zone?
output: A transition to mixed flow can occur due to a reduction in inflow velocity, a reduction in inflow aperture area, and the dominance of buoyancy effects.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Room Air Zone Is Recirculating Status indicate?
output: It indicates whether recirculations are present in the flow.

input: According to EnergyPlus, when does a cross ventilation flow not have recirculations?
output: A cross ventilation flow does not have recirculations whenever the inflow area is similar to the room cross section area.

input: In EnergyPlus, what integer values represent yes and no for recirculating status?
output: A value of 1 represents yes, and a value of 0 represents no.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the RoomAirSettings:UnderFloorAirDistributionInterior model?
output: The model is applicable to interior spaces that are served by an underfloor air distribution system.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the dominant sources of heat gain in the RoomAirSettings:UnderFloorAirDistributionInterior model?
output: The dominant sources of heat gain should be from people, equipment, and other localized sources located in the occupied part of the room.

input: According to EnergyPlus, when should the RoomAirSettings:UnderFloorAirDistributionInterior model be used with caution?

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the significance of the coefficient A in the formula for Kc?
output: The coefficient A is part of the formula Kc = A*Gamma**B + C + D*Gamma + E*Gamma**2, which characterizes the amount of stratification in a UFAD zone.

output: The default is autocalculate.

output: Coefficient C is part of the formula Kc = A*Gamma**B + C + D*Gamma + E*Gamma**2, which characterizes the amount of stratification in a UFAD zone.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the output for Room Air Zone Mixed Subzone Temperature measured in?
output: Room Air Zone Mixed Subzone Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius [C].

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the output for Room Air Zone Occupied Subzone Temperature represent?
output: The output for Room Air Zone Occupied Subzone Temperature represents the temperature of the lower, occupied subzone in degrees Celsius [C].

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the Room Air Zone Transition Height defined?
output: Room Air Zone Transition Height is defined as the height above the floor, in meters, of the boundary between the lower occupied subzone and the upper subzone.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Room Air Zone Is Mixed Status output indicate?
output: Room Air Zone Is Mixed Status is an integer flag that indicates whether the zone is mixed (single node well-mixed zone model used) or stratified (UCSD UFE model used), where 1 means well-mixed and 0 means stratified.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the Room Air Zone Average Temperature Gradient output measure?
output: The Room Air Zone Average Temperature Gradient output measures the temperature gradient between the middle of the occupied subzone and the middle of the upper subzone in degrees Kelvin per meter [K/m].

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the Room Air Zone Effective Comfort Air Temperature output represent?
output: Room Air Zone Effective Comfort Air Temperature represents the temperature at the user specified comfort height in degrees Celsius [C].

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the significance of the Room Air Zone Thermostat Temperature output?
output: Room Air Zone Thermostat Temperature output signifies the temperature at the height of the thermostat, as specified by user input, in degrees Celsius [C].

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the Room Air Zone Transition Height Gamma Value indicate?
output: Room Air Zone Transition Height Gamma Value is a dimensionless 'height' used in calculating the transition height, where lower values indicate increased stratification and higher values indicate less, generally ranging between 2 and 30.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the Room Air Zone Plume Heat Transfer Rate output measure?
output: Room Air Zone Plume Heat Transfer Rate measures the heat in watts driving the plumes in the occupied subzone.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Room Air Zone Window Plume Heat Transfer Rate output represent?
output: Room Air Zone Window Plume Heat Transfer Rate represents the convective heat gain from windows in an UnderFloorAirDistributionExterior zone, measured in watts [W].

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the Room Air Zone Temperature Stratification Fraction defined?
output: Room Air Zone Temperature Stratification Fraction, denoted as Phi, is a measure of temperature stratification in the space, calculated as the difference between the occupied subzone temperature and the supply temperature divided by the difference between the return temperature and the supply temperature.

input: What is the equation for the Room Air Zone Temperature Stratification Fraction in EnergyPlus?
output: In EnergyPlus, the Room Air Zone Temperature Stratification Fraction (Phi) is calculated as \\( \\fracT_occ - T_supT_ret - T_sup \\).

input: In EnergyPlus, what approach does the RoomAirflowNetwork model use to simulate a thermal zone?
output: The RoomAirflowNetwork model simulates a thermal zone using a network approach by assuming intra-zone nodes connected by user-defined patterns of airflows.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what capabilities does the RoomAirflowNetwork model provide regarding node connections?
output: The RoomAirflowNetwork model allows users to specify a node to be connected to surfaces to have convective heat transfer between surfaces and the node, along with a portion of internal gains and supply air and return air fractions from zone equipment.

input: In EnergyPlus, what objects are required for the RoomAirflowNetwork model to function properly?
output: The RoomAirflowNetwork model requires the following objects: RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork, RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork, RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:AdjacentSurfaceList, RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:InternalGains, RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:HVACEquipment, AirflowNetwork:Intrazone:Node, and AirflowNetwork:Intrazone:Linkage.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork object provide for the RoomAirflowNetwork model?
output: The RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork object provides inputs in a thermal zone needed for the RoomAirflowNetwork model, specifying a thermal zone and a list of RoomAir nodes.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork object in relation to model configuration?
output: The RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork object gives a summary of the model configuration in a zone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the significance of the 'Name' field in the RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork object?
output: The 'Name' field in the RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork object is a unique character string associated with this instance of the object.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the 'Zone Name' field represent in the RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork object?
output: The 'Zone Name' field represents the name of the EnergyPlus thermal zone corresponding to the RoomAir model zone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the role of the 'Control Point RoomAir:Node Name' field in the RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork object?
output: The 'Control Point RoomAir:Node Name' field specifies the name of a RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object that contains the sensor for zone HVAC controls, which will be used for thermostatic, humidistatic, or comfort-based control decisions.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is required for the zone node defined in a Zone object?
output: The zone node defined in a Zone object is required for the control decisions made by the RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork object.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object?
output: The RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object is used to define a node in a thermal zone, specifying the fraction of zone volume and providing a list of names to define fraction of internal gains, surface connection, and HVAC equipment.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what information does the Field: Name in the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object provide?
output: The Field: Name provides a unique character string associated with this instance of the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the Field: Zone Name specify in the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object?
output: The Field: Zone Name specifies the name of the EnergyPlus thermal zone and is defined in a RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Field: Fraction of Zone Air Volume indicate for the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object?
output: The Field: Fraction of Zone Air Volume specifies a fraction of the overall zone air volume that is assigned to this RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object, which is used to calculate the zone air storage term.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the function of the Field: RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:AdjacentSurfaceList Name?
output: The Field: RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:AdjacentSurfaceList Name specifies a name to provide a list of connected adjacent surfaces with convective heat transfer between the surfaces and this particular node.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the Field: RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:InternalGains Name define?
output: The Field: RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:InternalGains Name specifies a name to provide a list of internal gain objects and associated fractions assigned to this particular node.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Field: RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:HVACEquipment Name?
output: The Field: RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:HVACEquipment Name specifies a name to provide a list of HVAC equipment, including AirLoop terminals and zone equipment.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the fraction of internal gains and HVAC equipment related to the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object?
output: The RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork object will receive the fraction of internal gains and HVAC equipment, along with a list of surface names exposed to this node with convective heat transfer.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is an example of the input for the RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork object?

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:AdjacentSurfaceList object?
output: The RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:AdjacentSurfaceList object is used to provide a list of connected adjacent surfaces with convective heat transfer between surfaces and this particular node.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens when a moisture mode is assigned to surfaces within the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:AdjacentSurfaceList?
output: When a moisture mode is assigned to surfaces, convective moisture transfer will be calculated.

input: In EnergyPlus, what restriction is placed on the surface exposed to a particular node in the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:AdjacentSurfaceList?

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the 'Name' field represent in the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:AdjacentSurfaceList object?
output: The 'Name' field is a unique character string associated with this instance of the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:AdjacentSurfaceList object.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the 'Surface <#> Name' field specify in the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:AdjacentSurfaceList object?

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the function of the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:InternalGains object?

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the 'Name' field represent in the RoomAir:Node:AirflowNetwork:InternalGains object?

output: This group of objects describes other internal gains that may come into play, including People, Lights, and Various Equipment Types.

output: Each internal gains object has a field for 'Zone or ZoneList or Space or SpaceList Name'.

input: According to EnergyPlus, at what level are all internal gains modeled?
output: All internal gains are modeled at the Space level.

input: In EnergyPlus, how are names for internal gain input objects constructed?
output: Names are constructed using the <Object Name>, <Zone Name>, or <Space Name>.

input: What happens in EnergyPlus if the concatenated name of an internal gain exceeds 100 characters?
output: A warning will be shown and the name will be truncated.

input: In EnergyPlus, what occurs if the concatenated name of an internal gain duplicates another name?
output: There will be a severe error and the run will terminate.

input: According to EnergyPlus, for what purposes is the concatenated name used?
output: The concatenated name is used when referring to specific instances of internal gains for Output:Variables, Energy Management System (EMS) controls, and Demand Limiting Controls.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the result of specifying a Space Name for an internal gain?
output: It will result in one instance of the internal gain, named <Object Name>, with the full magnitude of the gain applied to the Space using the design level, space floor area, or space occupancy as appropriate.

input: What is the outcome in EnergyPlus when a SpaceList Name is used for an internal gain?
output: It will result in one instance of the internal gain for each Space in the SpaceList, named <Space Name> <Object Name>, with the full magnitude of the gain applied to each Space using the design level, space floor area, or space occupancy as appropriate.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does specifying a Zone Name affect the instances of an internal gain?
output: It will result in one instance of the internal gain for each Space in the Zone; if there is only one Space, it will be named <Object Name>, and if there is more than one Space, each instance will be named <Space Name> <Object Name>.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the full magnitude of the gain applied when using a Zone Name?
output: The full magnitude of the gain will be split between the Spaces in the Zone apportioned by the Space floor area or occupancy depending on the input method.

input: In EnergyPlus, what naming convention is used for instances of internal gain associated with Spaces in a ZoneList?
output: Each instance will be named <Space Name> <Object Name>.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the full magnitude of internal gain applied to Zones in a ZoneList?
output: The full magnitude of the gain will be applied to each Zone in the ZoneList then split between the Spaces in each Zone apportioned by the Space floor area or occupancy depending on the input method.

output: ElectricEquipment:ITE:AirCooled only allows Zone or Space Name.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the people statement?
output: The people statement is used to model the occupant’s effect on the space conditions.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what information does the people statement provide?
output: The people statement provides information that can be used to report the thermal comfort of a group of occupants.

input: In EnergyPlus, which thermal comfort models are available for use with the people statement?
output: The available thermal comfort models are the Fanger model, Pierce Two-Node model, Kansas State University Two-Node model, ASHRAE Standard 55 Elevated Air Cooling Effect model, and ASHRAE Standard 55 Ankle Draft Risk model.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how can a user select a thermal comfort model for a People statement?
output: A user may select any of the thermal comfort models by adding the appropriate choice keyword after the air velocity schedule name.

input: In EnergyPlus, when are thermal comfort calculations made for people statements?
output: Thermal comfort calculations will only be made for people statements that include specific requests for the thermal comfort models.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what input is required for zone carbon dioxide simulations in the people statement?
output: The input required is the carbon dioxide generation rate based on people activity level.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the requirement for the name of the People object?
output: The name of the People object must be unique across all People objects.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the field 'Zone or ZoneList or Space or SpaceList Name' apply to?
output: This field applies the People object to one or more thermal zones or spaces in the building.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how can the Zone, Zonelist, or SpaceList options be used with the Number of People Calculation Method?
output: The Zone, Zonelist, or SpaceList options can be used effectively with the people/area and area/person options of the Number of People Calculation Method to place a varying number of people at the same density in each zone or space.

input: From EnergyPlus, how should the names of actual people objects be formatted?
output: The names of the actual people objects may be concatenated as <Space Name> <People Object Name>.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens when multiple people objects are defined for the same zone with different SET, PMV, or Heat/Cold Stress Temperature Threshold?
output: A warning message will be produced to caution users that zone-level resilience metrics results will only be meaningful if each zone has at most one People object defined.

input: According to EnergyPlus, why might the zone-level resilience metrics results be invalid when multiple people objects are linked to one zone?
output: This is because in the calculation of zone level Heating/Cooling SET Degree-Hours, if multiple People objects are defined for one zone, EnergyPlus will only use the SET of one People object to compute the zone level SET Degree-Hours, neglecting the SET of other people objects defined in the same zone.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the significance of the field 'Number of People Schedule Name'?
output: This field is the name of the schedule that modifies the number of people parameter.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the actual number of people in a zone calculated according to the 'Number of People Schedule Name' field?
output: The actual number of people in a zone is the product of the number of people field and the value of the schedule specified by name in this field.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the 'Number of People Calculation Method' field describe?
output: This field is a key/choice field that tells which of the next three fields are filled and is descriptive of the method for calculating the nominal number of occupants in the Zone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the 'People' choice in the Number of People Calculation Method indicate?
output: With this choice, the method used will be a straight insertion of the number of occupants.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the 'People/Area' choice in the Number of People Calculation Method entail?
output: With this choice, the method used will be a factor per floor area of the zone or space.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the 'Area/Person' choice in the Number of People Calculation Method refer to?
output: With this choice, the method used will be a factor of floor area per person.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the field 'Number of People' represent?
output: The field 'Number of People' represents the maximum number of people in a zone that is then multiplied by a schedule fraction.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does the 'Number of People' field allow for flexibility?
output: In EnergyPlus, the 'Number of People' field allows for flexibility by being able to apply a 'diversity factor' to a schedule of real numbers.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is noted about the schedule value in relation to the 'Number of People' field?
output: The schedule value can vary from hour to hour, while the 'Number of People' field is constant for all simulation environments.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the 'People per Floor Area' field?
output: The 'People per Floor Area' field is used, along with the Zone or Space Floor Area, to determine the maximum number of people as described in the 'Number of People' field.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what unit is used for the 'People per Floor Area' factor?
output: The unit used for the 'People per Floor Area' factor is person/m².

input: In EnergyPlus, what method should be chosen for the 'People per Floor Area' field?
output: The method chosen for the 'People per Floor Area' field should be 'people/area'.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the 'Floor Area per Person' field represent?
output: The 'Floor Area per Person' field represents a factor (m²/person) used along with the Zone or Space Floor Area to determine the maximum number of people as described in the 'Number of People' field.

input: In EnergyPlus, what method should be selected for the 'Floor Area per Person' field?
output: The method selected for the 'Floor Area per Person' field should be 'area/person'.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the range of the Fraction Radiant field?
output: The Fraction Radiant field is a decimal number between 0.0 and 1.0.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the Fraction Radiant field used in relation to heat emitted by people in a zone?
output: The number specified in the Fraction Radiant field will be multiplied by the total sensible energy emitted by people to give the amount of long wavelength radiation gain from human beings in a zone.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is assumed about the remainder of the sensible load when calculating radiant gains from people?
output: The remainder of the sensible load is assumed to be convective heat gain.

input: In EnergyPlus, are latent gains from people included in the radiant or convective heat gains?
output: No, latent gains from people are not included in either the radiant or convective heat gains.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Fraction Radiant field?
output: The default value for the Fraction Radiant field is 0.30.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Sensible Heat Fraction field allow the user to specify?
output: The Sensible Heat Fraction field allows the user to specify a fixed sensible fraction for the heat gain due to the PEOPLE object.

input: From EnergyPlus, how does the program typically calculate the sensible/latent split for heat gains?
output: Normally, the program calculates the sensible/latent split automatically.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if the Sensible Heat Fraction field is left blank or set to autocalculate?
output: If the Sensible Heat Fraction field is blank or set to autocalculate, the program will calculate the sensible/latent split.

input: In EnergyPlus, what occurs if a value is entered in the Sensible Heat Fraction field?
output: If a value is entered in the Sensible Heat Fraction field, it will be used as the sensible fraction of the current total heat gain.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Activity Level Schedule Name field?
output: The Activity Level Schedule Name field determines the amount of heat gain per person in the zone under design conditions.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does heat gain from the Activity Level Schedule impact the zone?
output: The heat gain impacts the basic zone heat balance as well as the modeling of thermal comfort.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the heat gain value modified in relation to space temperature?
output: The heat gain value is modified based on a correlation to account for variations in space temperature.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the units for the Activity Level Schedule values?
output: The units for the Activity Level Schedule values are Watts per person.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what types of heat gain are included in the total heat gain per person?
output: The total heat gain per person includes convective, radiant, and latent heat gains.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the sensible portion of total heat gain determined?
output: An internal algorithm is used to determine what fraction of the total heat gain is sensible and what fraction is latent.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the radiant and convective portion of sensible heat gain calculated?
output: The sensible portion is divided into radiant and convective portions using the value specified for Fraction Radiant.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the typical range of activity level values for most office activities?
output: The typical range of activity level values for most office activities is approximately 100-150 Watts per person.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the maximum activity level value for strenuous physical activities?
output: The maximum activity level value for strenuous physical activities can exceed 900 Watts per person.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens when the activity level schedule values fall outside normal ranges?
output: Warnings are produced when the activity level schedule values fall outside normal ranges.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the default carbon dioxide generation rate per person?
output: The default carbon dioxide generation rate per person is 3.82E-8 m3/s-W.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the total carbon dioxide generation rate calculated?
output: The total carbon dioxide generation rate is calculated as Number of People * People Schedule * People Activity * Carbon Dioxide Generation Rate.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the maximum allowable carbon dioxide generation rate compared to the default value?
output: The maximum value can be 10 times the default carbon dioxide generation rate.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Cold Stress Temperature Threshold field?
output: The Cold Stress Temperature Threshold field is used in the calculation of hours of safety for cold events.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the longest duration for cold events defined?
output: The longest duration is defined as the number of hours starting from the beginning time of the risk period to not below a certain temperature threshold.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default temperature threshold if not specified for cold stress?
output: If not specified, the default temperature threshold is 60F (or 15.56C).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Heat Stress Temperature Threshold field?
output: The Heat Stress Temperature Threshold field is used in the calculation of hours of safety for hot events, defined as the longest duration starting from the beginning time of the risk period to not above a certain temperature threshold.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what default temperature threshold is used if the Heat Stress Temperature Threshold is not specified?
output: If not specified, 86F (or 30C) will be used as the default temperature threshold.

input: In EnergyPlus, what values can the field Enable ASHRAE 55 comfort warnings accept?
output: The field Enable ASHRAE 55 comfort warnings accepts either 'Yes' or 'No' as values.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens when 'Yes' is specified in the Enable ASHRAE 55 comfort warnings field?
output: When 'Yes' is specified, warnings are generated when the space conditions are outside of the ASHRAE 55 comfort range.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Enable ASHRAE 55 comfort warnings field?
output: The default is not to provide these warnings, so if you want to know if your space is outside this comfort range, you must set this field to Yes.

output: The activity level met for Sleeping with a Schedule Value of 72 W/Person is 0.7.
