output: The default value for the Economizer Lockout field is 'NoLockout'.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Economizer Upper Temperature Limit field?
output: The Economizer Upper Temperature Limit field is used to enter the outdoor air temperature high limit for economizer operation; if the outdoor air temperature exceeds this limit, the outdoor airflow rate is set to minimum.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does entering zero in the Economizer Upper Temperature Limit field signify?
output: Entering zero in the Economizer Upper Temperature Limit field means that there is no outdoor air temperature high limit control.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Economizer Lower Temperature Limit field?
output: The Economizer Lower Temperature Limit field sets the outdoor air temperature low limit for economizer operation; if the outdoor air temperature is below this limit, the outdoor air flow rate will be set to the minimum and heat recovery will be enabled if available.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if there is no input or zero in the Economizer Lower Temperature Limit field?
output: No input or zero in the Economizer Lower Temperature Limit field means that there is no outdoor air temperature low limit control.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Economizer Upper Enthalpy Limit field define?
output: The Economizer Upper Enthalpy Limit field defines the outdoor air upper enthalpy limit for economizer operation; if the outdoor air enthalpy is above this value, the outdoor air flow rate will be set to the minimum and heat recovery will be enabled if available.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the implication of having no input or zero in the Economizer Upper Enthalpy Limit field?
output: No input or zero in the Economizer Upper Enthalpy Limit field means that there is no outdoor air enthalpy limit control.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the function of the Economizer Maximum Limit Dewpoint Temperature field?
output: The Economizer Maximum Limit Dewpoint Temperature field is used to input the outdoor air dewpoint limit for economizer operation; if the outdoor air dewpoint temperature is above this value, the outdoor airflow rate will be set to the minimum.

input: According to EnergyPlus, when is the Economizer Maximum Limit Dewpoint Temperature field required?
output: This field is required if the Economizer Control Type ‘FixedDewPointAndDryBulb’ has been specified.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does it mean if there is no input in the Economizer Maximum Limit Dewpoint Temperature field?
output: No input (blank) in the Economizer Maximum Limit Dewpoint Temperature field means that there is no outdoor air dewpoint limit control.

input: In EnergyPlus, how should the Supply Plenum Name field be handled if no supply plenum is to be modeled?
output: The Supply Plenum Name field should be set to blank if no supply plenum is to be modeled.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how must a modeled supply plenum be defined?
output: If a supply plenum is modeled, it must be modeled as a zone with surfaces, and the name of the plenum zone should be entered in the Supply Plenum Name field.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the role of the supply plenum in the system?
output: The supply plenum serves all zones on this system; if any supply plenums have been specified, the outlet from the system supply plenum will flow through the supply plenum to the zone terminal unit.

input: In EnergyPlus, what should be done if no return plenum is to be modeled?
output: The Return Plenum Name field should be set to blank if no return plenum is to be modeled.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is a return plenum required to be modeled?
output: If a return plenum is modeled, it must be modeled as a zone with surfaces, and the name of the plenum zone should be entered in the Return Plenum Name field.

input: In EnergyPlus, what function does the return plenum serve in the system?
output: The return plenum serves all zones on this system; if any zone return plenums have been specified, the return air from the zone will flow through the zone return plenum and then into the system return plenum.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the two choices for the Supply Fan Placement field?
output: The two choices for the Supply Fan Placement field are DrawThrough and BlowThrough.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does the DrawThrough placement type for the supply fan function?
output: DrawThrough models a system where the supply air fan is after the cooling and heating coils.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the BlowThrough placement type for the supply fan indicate?
output: BlowThrough models a system where the supply air fan is before the cooling and heating coils.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Supply Fan Placement field?
output: The default setting for the Supply Fan Placement field is DrawThrough.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Supply Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients field?
output: The purpose of the Supply Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients field is to select the set of generic pre-defined coefficients to use for the supply fan part-load power consumption.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the choices available for the supply fan part-load power consumption coefficients?
output: The choices available for the supply fan part-load power consumption coefficients are InletVaneDampers, OutletDampers, VariableSpeedMotor, ASHRAE90.1-2004Appendix G, and VariableSpeedMotorPressureReset.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the supply fan part-load power coefficients?
output: The default setting for the supply fan part-load power coefficients is InletVaneDampers.

input: In EnergyPlus, where can the resulting power curves for the supply fan part-load power coefficients be found?
output: The resulting power curves for the supply fan part-load power coefficients can be found in Figure 10.7, VAV Supply Fan Part-Load Power Coefficient Options.

input: According to EnergyPlus, where do the ASHRAE 90.1-2004 Appendix G coefficients come from?
output: The ASHRAE 90.1-2004 Appendix G coefficients come from TABLE G3.1.3.15, Method 2.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the source of the coefficients for the other sets besides ASHRAE 90.1-2004 Appendix G?
output: The other sets of coefficients are from the EnergyPlus Input Output Reference, Fan Coefficient Values table.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the basis for the VariableSpeedMotorPressureReset option?
output: The VariableSpeedMotorPressureReset option is based on Good Static Pressure Reset VSD Fan from Energy Design Resources’: Design Guidelines: Advanced Variable Air Volume (VAV) Systems (EDR_DesignGuidelines_VAV.pdf).

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the possible inputs for the Night Cycle Control field when the System Availability Schedule is zero?
output: The possible inputs are StayOff, CycleOnAny, CycleOnControl Zone, or CycleOnAnyZoneFansOnly.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does StayOff mean in the context of Night Cycle Control?
output: StayOff means the system will remain off, no matter how hot or cold the zones may be.

input: From EnergyPlus, what occurs when CycleOnAny is selected for Night Cycle Control?
output: CycleOnAny means that if any zone served by this system has an air temperature outside the cooling or heating set points, the central fan will turn on even though the System Availability Schedule indicates the fan is off.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does CycleOnControlZone differ from CycleOnAny in Night Cycle Control?
output: CycleOnControlZone means the availability manager looks at the temperature in only the zone specified in Night Cycle Control Zone Name, whereas CycleOnAny considers temperatures in all zones served by the system.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the function of CycleOnAnyZoneFansOnly in Night Cycle Control?
output: CycleOnAnyZoneFansOnly is the same as CycleOnAny except that only the zone fans are cycled on and the central air handler fan is left off, applicable only if using HVACTemplate:Zone:VAV:FanPowered in one or more zones.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Night Cycle Control field?
output: The default is StayOff.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is required for the Night Cycle Control Zone Name field?
output: For the Night Cycle Control option Cycle On Control Zone, enter the name of the control zone; for other Night Cycle Control options, this field is ignored.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what types of air-to-air heat recovery can be selected in the Heat Recovery Type field?
output: The choices are None, Sensible, and Enthalpy.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Heat Recovery Type field?
output: The default is None.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the valid range for the Sensible Heat Recovery Effectiveness?
output: The valid range is from 0.0 to 1.0, and the default is 0.70.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Latent Heat Recovery Effectiveness field?
output: Enter the latent heat recovery effectiveness if Heat Recovery Type is Enthalpy; this is applied as a constant effectiveness at all conditions.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the valid range for the Latent Heat Recovery Effectiveness?
output: The valid range is from 0.0 to 1.0, and the default is 0.65.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type field allow you to select?
output: The Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type field allows you to select the type of automatic reset control for the cooling supply air temperature.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens when the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type is set to 'None'?
output: When set to 'None', there is no reset, and the system uses the Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule or Cooling Coil Design Setpoint.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the 'Warmest' Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type do?
output: The 'Warmest' reset type sets the cooling supply air temperature to the highest supply air temperature that will meet the cooling requirements of all the zones at the maximum supply air flow rate, with a minimum setpoint of the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the maximum setpoint allowed when using the 'Warmest' reset type?
output: The maximum setpoint allowed when using the 'Warmest' reset type is defaulted to the greater of 18C or the Heating Coil Design Setpoint plus 1.0C.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does the 'OutdoorAirTemperatureReset' reset type affect the cooling supply air temperature?
output: The 'OutdoorAirTemperatureReset' type adjusts the cooling supply air temperature based on outdoor dry-bulb temperature, with specific setpoints defined for temperatures at or below 15.6C and at or above 26.7C, and a linear variation in between.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the setpoint for the 'OutdoorAirTemperatureReset' when the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or below 15.6C?
output: When the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or below 15.6C, the setpoint is the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint plus 5.2C.

input: What is the setpoint for the 'OutdoorAirTemperatureReset' in EnergyPlus when the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or above 26.7C?
output: When the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or above 26.7C, the setpoint is the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the 'WarmestTemperatureFirst' reset type do?
output: The 'WarmestTemperatureFirst' reset type finds the highest setpoint temperature that will satisfy all the zone cooling loads at minimum supply air flow rate, and if this temperature is less than the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint, it sets the temperature to the minimum and increases the supply air flow rate to meet the loads.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the maximum setpoint allowed for the 'WarmestTemperatureFirst' reset type?
output: The maximum setpoint allowed for the 'WarmestTemperatureFirst' reset type is defaulted to the greater of 18C or the Heating Coil Design Setpoint plus 1.0C.

input: What is the default setting for the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type in EnergyPlus?
output: The default setting for the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type in EnergyPlus is 'None'.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the options available for the Heating Coil Setpoint Reset Type?
output: The options available are None, which uses the Heating Coil Setpoint Schedule or Heating Coil Design Setpoint, and OutdoorAirTemperatureReset, which resets the heating supply air temperature based on outdoor dry-bulb temperature.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Heating Coil Setpoint Reset Type?
output: The default setting for the Heating Coil Setpoint Reset Type is None.

input: From EnergyPlus, what happens to the heating supply air temperature setpoint when the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or below –6.7C?
output: When the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or below –6.7C, the setpoint is the Heating Coil Design Setpoint.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the behavior of the heating supply air temperature setpoint when the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or above 10.0C?
output: When the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or above 10.0C, the setpoint is the Heating Coil Design Setpoint minus 5.2C.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the two options available for Dehumidification Control Type?
output: The two options available for Dehumidification Control Type are None and CoolReheat.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the CoolReheat option do?
output: The CoolReheat option cools beyond the dry-bulb setpoint as required to meet the humidity setpoint if the system is capable of doing so, with reheat provided as required by the terminal unit reheat coils if available.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for Dehumidification Control Type?
output: The default setting for Dehumidification Control Type is None.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Dehumidification Control Zone Name field specify?
output: The Dehumidification Control Zone Name field specifies the zone name where the humidistat is located for controlling dehumidification.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Dehumidification Setpoint?
output: The default value for the Dehumidification Setpoint is 60%.

input: In EnergyPlus, what types of humidifiers are available for selection?
output: The types of humidifiers available are None and ElectricSteam.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the ElectricSteam humidifier option utilize?
output: The ElectricSteam humidifier option uses the Humidifier:Steam:Electric object.

input: From EnergyPlus, what happens if the Humidifier Availability Schedule Name field is left blank?
output: If the Humidifier Availability Schedule Name field is left blank, the humidifier will be available anytime the system is operating.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the availability of the humidifier defined if a schedule name is specified?
output: If a schedule name is specified, it defines when the humidifier is available, with a schedule value of 1.0 indicating that the humidifier can be on during a given time period and a value of zero indicating that it cannot be used.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default rated moisture output rate for the humidifier?
output: The default rated moisture output rate for the humidifier is 0.000001 m3/s.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the Humidifier Rated Electric Power determined?
output: The Humidifier Rated Electric Power is determined at the rated capacity moisture output and can be autosized based on the rated capacity in kg/s and the enthalpy rise in J/kg of the feed water from a reference temperature of liquid water at 20°C to saturated steam at 100°C.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the Humidifier Control Zone Name field specify?
output: The Humidifier Control Zone Name field specifies the zone name where the humidistat is located for controlling humidification.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Humidifier Setpoint?
output: The default value for the Humidifier Setpoint is 30%.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Sizing Option field specify?
output: The Sizing Option field specifies the sizing method for the system supply air flow rate.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the two sizing methods available for the system supply air flow rate?
output: The two sizing methods available are Coincident sizes on the sum of the coincident zone supply air flow rates and NonCoincident sizes on the sum of the noncoincident zone design supply air flow rates.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Sizing Option field?
output: The default setting for the Sizing Option field is NonCoincident.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how should the Return Fan field be filled out if the system has a return fan?
output: Enter Yes if the system has a return fan; the default is No.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Return Fan Total Efficiency field represent?
output: The Return Fan Total Efficiency field represents the ratio of the power delivered to the air to the electrical input power at maximum flow.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the Return Fan Total Efficiency calculated?
output: The Return Fan Total Efficiency is calculated as the product of the fan motor efficiency and fan (impeller) efficiency.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the definition of motor efficiency for the return fan?
output: The motor efficiency is defined as the power delivered to the shaft divided by the electrical power input to the motor.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is fan efficiency defined?
output: Fan efficiency is defined as the power delivered to the air divided by the shaft power.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the power delivered to the fluid calculated for the return fan?
output: The power delivered to the fluid is calculated as the mass flow rate of the air multiplied by the pressure rise divided by the air density.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the constraints on the Return Fan Total Efficiency value?
output: The Return Fan Total Efficiency must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 1.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Return Fan Delta Pressure field require?
output: The Return Fan Delta Pressure field requires the pressure rise in Pa at full flow and standard conditions.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the standard conditions for the Return Fan Delta Pressure?
output: Standard conditions for the Return Fan Delta Pressure are considered to be 20 degrees Celsius at sea level, 101325 Pa.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Return Fan Delta Pressure?
output: The default value for the Return Fan Delta Pressure is 500 Pa.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the Return Fan Motor efficiency defined?
output: The Return Fan Motor efficiency is defined as the shaft power of the return fan divided by the electrical power consumed.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the constraints on the Return Fan Motor efficiency value?
output: The Return Fan Motor efficiency must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 1.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the Return Fan Motor in Air Stream Fraction field represent?
output: The Return Fan Motor in Air Stream Fraction field represents the fraction of the motor heat that is added to the air stream.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does a value of 0 indicate for the Return Fan Motor in Air Stream Fraction?
output: A value of 0 indicates that the motor is completely outside the air stream.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does a value of 1 indicate for the Return Fan Motor in Air Stream Fraction?
output: A value of 1 indicates that all of the motor heat will go into the air stream and act to cause a temperature rise.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the acceptable range for the Return Fan Motor in Air Stream Fraction?
output: The acceptable range for the Return Fan Motor in Air Stream Fraction is between 0 and 1.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Return Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients field?
output: The Return Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients field is used to select the set of generic pre-defined coefficients for the return fan part-load power consumption.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the choices available for the Return Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients?
output: The choices available for the Return Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients are InletVaneDampers, OutletDampers, VariableSpeedMotor, ASHRAE90.1-2004Appendix G, and VariableSpeedMotorPressureReset.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Return Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients?
output: The default setting for the Return Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients is InletVaneDampers.

input: In EnergyPlus, where can the resulting power curves for the Return Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients be found?
output: The resulting power curves for the Return Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients are shown in Figure 10.7.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what source provides the ASHRAE 90.1-2004 Appendix G coefficients?
output: The ASHRAE 90.1-2004 Appendix G coefficients are from TABLE G3.1.3.15, Method 2.

input: In EnergyPlus, where are the other sets of coefficients for the Return Fan Part-Load Power Coefficients derived from?
output: The other sets of coefficients are derived from the EnergyPlus Input Output Reference, Fan Coefficient Values table.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the basis for the VariableSpeedMotorPressureReset option?
output: The VariableSpeedMotorPressureReset option is based on Good Static Pressure Reset VSD Fan from Energy Design Resources’: Design Guidelines: Advanced Variable Air Volume (VAV) Systems.

output: A schedule value of zero denotes that the cooling coil cannot be used during that time period.

input: In EnergyPlus, what should be done to specify a constant setpoint for the cooling coil?
output: Leave the Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule Name field blank, and the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint value will be used at all times.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule?
output: The Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule is used to specify the schedule name that controls the supply air temperature delivered to the zones.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does the fan placement affect the leaving air temperature from the cooling coil?
output: For Blow Through fan placement, the leaving air temperature is from the cooling coil, while for Draw Through fan placement, it is the leaving air temperature after the supply fan.

input: According to EnergyPlus, in what units are the values in the Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule expressed?
output: The values in the Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule are in degrees Celsius.

input: In EnergyPlus, when is the Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule field ignored?
output: The Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule field is ignored if the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type is something other than None.

input: What is the default value for the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type in EnergyPlus?
output: The default value for the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type is None.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint used for?
output: The Cooling Coil Design Setpoint is used for sizing the cooling coil and zone supply air flow rates.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default cooling supply air temperature for the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint?
output: The default cooling supply air temperature for the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint is 12.8 degrees Celsius.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens if no Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule or Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type is specified?
output: If no Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule or Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type is specified, the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint value is used as a constant cooling supply air setpoint temperature.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does entering 'Autosize' for the Cooling Coil Gross Rated Total Capacity do?
output: Entering 'Autosize' allows the automatic sizing algorithm to determine the cooling coil gross rated total capacity based on the maximum cooling loads during the cooling design day.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does a user-entered value for Cooling Coil Gross Rated Total Capacity represent?
output: A user-entered value represents the full load gross total cooling capacity, including both sensible and latent capacity, in watts of the DX coil unit at rated conditions.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the assumed low-speed capacity for Cooling Coil Type = TwoSpeedDX?
output: For Cooling Coil Type = TwoSpeedDX, the low-speed capacity is assumed to be 0.33 times the gross rated total capacity.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the assumed stage 1 capacity for Cooling Coil Type = TwoSpeedHumidControlDX?
output: For Cooling Coil Type = TwoSpeedHumidControlDX, the stage 1 capacity is assumed to be 0.5 times the gross rated total capacity.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the rated conditions for the cooling coil?
output: The rated conditions are air entering the cooling coil at the maximum supply air flow rate at 26.7°C drybulb/19.4°C wetbulb with air entering the outdoor condenser coil at 35°C drybulb.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the capacity of the cooling coil defined regarding supply air fan heat?
output: The capacity should be the 'gross', meaning the effect of supply air fan heat is not accounted for.

input: From EnergyPlus, what are the units used for the Cooling Coil Gross Rated Total Capacity?
output: The units for the Cooling Coil Gross Rated Total Capacity are in watts (W).

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for Cooling Coil Gross Rated Total Capacity?
output: The default setting for Cooling Coil Gross Rated Total Capacity is 'Autosize'.

input: In EnergyPlus, what should be entered to allow the sizing algorithm to determine the sensible heat ratio for the cooling coil?
output: Enter Autosize to allow the sizing algorithm to determine the sensible heat ratio based on the rated capacity and air flow rate.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the sensible heat ratio calculated if not using Autosize?
output: The value is the ratio of the gross sensible capacity divided by the gross total cooling capacity of the DX cooling coil at rated conditions.

input: From EnergyPlus, what are the rated conditions for the cooling coil's sensible heat ratio?
output: Rated conditions are air entering the cooling coil at the maximum supply air flow rate at 26.7°C drybulb/19.4°C wetbulb with air entering the outdoor condenser coil at 35°C drybulb.

input: In EnergyPlus, what type of cooling capacities should be used to define the Rated Sensible Heat Ratio (SHR)?
output: Both the sensible and total cooling capacities used to define the Rated Sensible Heat Ratio (SHR) should be 'gross', meaning the effect of supply air fan heat is not accounted for.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Cooling Coil Gross Rated Sensible Heat Ratio?
output: The default is Autosize.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the coefficient of performance (COP) for the cooling coil defined?
output: The coefficient of performance (COP) for the cooling coil is defined as the gross cooling coil capacity in watts divided by the electrical power input in watts of the DX cooling coil unit at rated conditions.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the rated conditions for measuring the cooling coil COP?
output: The rated conditions for measuring the cooling coil COP are air entering the cooling coil at the maximum supply air flow rate at 26.7°C drybulb/19.4°C wetbulb with air entering the outdoor condenser coil at 35°C drybulb.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the input power for the cooling coil include?
output: The input power for the cooling coil includes electric power for the compressor and condenser fan but does not include the power consumption of the supply air fan.

input: In EnergyPlus, should the gross COP account for the supply air fan?
output: The gross COP should not account for the supply air fan.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the cooling coil gross rated COP?
output: The default value for the cooling coil gross rated COP is 3.0.

input: In EnergyPlus, what types of heating can be used in the unitary system?
output: The types of heating that can be used in the unitary system are Electric, Gas, and HotWater.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Heating Coil Availability Schedule Name field?
output: The Heating Coil Availability Schedule Name field is usually set to blank, allowing the heating coil to be available anytime the system is operating.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if a schedule name is specified for the Heating Coil Availability Schedule?
output: If a schedule name is specified, it defines when the coil is available, which is most often used when heating is only available seasonally.

input: In EnergyPlus, how do schedule values affect the operation of the heating coil?
output: The schedule values denote whether the heating coil can run during a given time period.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does a schedule value of 1.0 indicate for the heating coil?
output: A schedule value of 1.0 indicates that the heating coil can be on during a given time period.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does a schedule value of zero signify for the heating coil's operation?
output: A schedule value of zero denotes that the heating coil cannot be used during that time period.

input: In EnergyPlus, what should be done if a constant setpoint for the heating coil is to be specified?
output: Leave the Heating Coil Setpoint Schedule Name field blank, and the Heating Coil Design Setpoint value will be used at all times.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the Heating Coil Setpoint Schedule control?
output: The Heating Coil Setpoint Schedule controls the supply air temperature delivered to the zones.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the leaving air temperature for Blow Through fan placement?
output: For Blow Through fan placement, the leaving air temperature is from the heating coil.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the leaving air temperature determined for Draw Through fan placement?
output: For Draw Through fan placement, the leaving air temperature is after the supply fan.

input: In EnergyPlus, what units are used for the values in the Heating Coil Setpoint Schedule?
output: The values in the schedule are in degrees Celsius (°C).

input: According to EnergyPlus, when is the Heating Coil Setpoint Schedule ignored?
output: This field is ignored if the Heating Coil Setpoint Reset Type is something other than None.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is entered in the Heating Coil Design Setpoint field?
output: The heating supply air temperature in degrees Celsius (°C) to be used for sizing the heating coil and zone supply air flow rates.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if no Heating Coil Setpoint Schedule or Heating Coil Setpoint Reset Type is specified?
output: The Heating Coil Design Setpoint value is used as a constant heating supply air setpoint temperature.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Heating Coil Design Setpoint?
output: The default value is 10.0°C.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does entering 'Autosize' in the Heating Coil Capacity field do?
output: It allows the sizing algorithm to determine the proper capacity required based on the loads experienced during the heating design day.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does a specified value in the Heating Coil Capacity field represent?
output: It represents the maximum amount of heat that the coil can deliver in Watts.

input: In EnergyPlus, how should the gas burner efficiency be entered in the Gas Heating Coil Efficiency field?
output: It should be entered as a decimal, not as a percent; for example, an 80% efficient burner would be entered as 0.8.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default entry for the Gas Heating Coil Efficiency field?
output: The default entry is 0.8.

input: In EnergyPlus, what should be entered in the Gas Heating Coil Parasitic Electric Load field?
output: The parasitic electric load associated with the gas heating coil operation, such as a combustion fan, measured in Watts.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Gas Heating Coil Parasitic Electric Load?
output: The default is 0.0 W.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Maximum Outdoor Air Flow Rate field?
output: It defines the maximum amount of outdoor air flow into the unit when the economizer is operating.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does entering 'Autosize' in the Maximum Outdoor Air Flow Rate field signify?
output: It means that 100% of the full supply flow may be taken from outdoor air.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens if a value is entered in the Maximum Outdoor Air Flow Rate field instead of Autosize?
output: The entered value is used instead of the autosize value.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what units are used for the Maximum Outdoor Air Flow Rate?
output: The units are in cubic meters per second (m3/s).

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Maximum Outdoor Air Flow Rate?
output: The default is Autosize.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Minimum Outdoor Air Flow Rate field?
output: The Minimum Outdoor Air Flow Rate field is used to enter Autosize or the value for the minimum amount of outdoor air that can enter the unit and be distributed to the zones.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the value for Minimum Outdoor Air Flow Rate typically determined?
output: The value is usually set to autosize and calculated by the outdoor air requirements of each zone.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens if a value is entered for the Minimum Outdoor Air Flow Rate?
output: If a value is entered, it overrides the outdoor air specification from the zone level.

input: What are the units for the Minimum Outdoor Air Flow Rate in EnergyPlus?
output: The units for the Minimum Outdoor Air Flow Rate are in m3/s.

input: What is the default setting for the Minimum Outdoor Air Flow Rate in EnergyPlus?
output: The default setting for the Minimum Outdoor Air Flow Rate is Autosize.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the significance of the Minimum Outdoor Air Control Type field?
output: The Minimum Outdoor Air Control Type field determines whether the minimum outdoor air flow rate is fixed or varies with the total system air flow rate.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the two choices for Minimum Outdoor Air Control Type?
output: The two choices for Minimum Outdoor Air Control Type are FixedMinimum and ProportionalMinimum.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does FixedMinimum mean for Minimum Outdoor Air Control Type?
output: FixedMinimum means that the minimum outdoor air flow rate is fixed no matter what the actual system flow rate is.

input: What does ProportionalMinimum signify in the context of EnergyPlus?
output: ProportionalMinimum means the minimum outdoor air flow rate varies in proportion to the total system air flow rate.

input: What is the default setting for Minimum Outdoor Air Control Type in EnergyPlus?
output: The default setting for Minimum Outdoor Air Control Type is ProportionalMinimum.

input: In EnergyPlus, what should be done with the Minimum Outdoor Air Schedule Name field if uniform outdoor air is desired throughout the year?
output: The Minimum Outdoor Air Schedule Name field should be left blank if the minimum outdoor air is to be the same for all hours in the entire year.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how are values specified in the Minimum Outdoor Air Schedule Name field interpreted?
output: If a schedule name is specified, values are decimal fractions (0.0 – 1.0) that multiply the minimum outdoor air flow rate.

input: What is the purpose of the schedule associated with the Minimum Outdoor Air Schedule Name in EnergyPlus?
output: The schedule is useful for reducing the outdoor air flow rate to zero during unoccupied or startup hours.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the available options for the Economizer Type field?
output: The available options for the Economizer Type field are ‘FixedDryBulb’, ‘DifferentialDryBulb’, ‘FixedEnthalpy’, ‘DifferentialEnthalpy’, ‘ElectronicEnthalpy’, ‘FixedDewPointAndDryBulb’, ‘DifferentialDryBulbAndEnthalpy’, and ‘NoEconomizer’.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens when 'NoEconomizer' is selected for the Economizer Type?
output: 'NoEconomizer' means the economizer will not operate and the outdoor airflow rate will be at the minimum for the entire simulation.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does selecting 'FixedDryBulb' affect outdoor airflow rate?
output: Choosing 'FixedDryBulb' means the economizer will set the outdoor airflow rate at minimum if the outdoor air temperature is higher than a specified dry-bulb temperature limit.

input: From EnergyPlus, what condition triggers the outdoor airflow to minimum when 'DifferentialDryBulb' is selected?
output: Choosing 'DifferentialDryBulb' will trigger the outdoor airflow to minimum when the dry-bulb temperature of outdoor air is higher than the dry-bulb temperature of the return air.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the 'FixedEnthalpy' economizer control strategy check?
output: 'FixedEnthalpy' checks the upper limit of the enthalpy given as a field input against the enthalpy content of outdoor air and will set the outdoor airflow rate to minimum if the latter is greater than the former.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how does 'DifferentialEnthalpy' operate?
output: 'DifferentialEnthalpy' compares the return air enthalpy with the enthalpy of outdoor air, and when the enthalpy of outdoor air is greater than the enthalpy of the return air, the outdoor air flow rate is set to minimum.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does selecting 'ElectronicEnthalpy' allow the simulation to calculate?
output: Choosing 'ElectronicEnthalpy' enables the simulation to calculate the humidity ratio limit of outdoor air based on the dry-bulb temperature of outdoor air and a quadratic/cubic curve.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the condition for setting the outdoor airflow rate to minimum when using 'FixedDewPointAndDryBulb'?
output: 'FixedDewPointAndDryBulb' compares both the outdoor dewpoint temperature and the outdoor dry-bulb temperature to their specified high limit values, and if either outdoor temperature exceeds the high limit value, the outdoor airflow rate is set to minimum.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does 'DifferentialDryBulbAndEnthalpy' enable in terms of economizer control strategies?
output: 'DifferentialDryBulbAndEnthalpy' enables the control strategy to be based on both the DifferentialDryBulb and DifferentialEnthalpy economizer control strategies.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what checks are performed by each economizer control type?
output: Each control type checks for user-entered values for the upper limit of dry-bulb temperature, enthalpy limit, humidity ratio limit, and dewpoint limit, setting the outdoor air flow rate to minimum if any of these entered limits are exceeded.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Economizer Type field?
output: The default for the Economizer Type field is 'NoEconomizer'.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the possible choices for the Economizer Lockout field?
output: The possible choices for the Economizer Lockout field are NoLockout, LockoutWithHeating, and LockoutWithCompressor.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the LockoutWithHeating option mean for economizer operation?
output: The LockoutWithHeating option means that if the packaged unit is in heating mode, the economizer is locked out, meaning the economizer dampers are closed and there is minimum outdoor air flow.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the LockoutWithCompressor option entail regarding the economizer's operation?
output: The LockoutWithCompressor option means that the economizer is locked out when the unit is in heating mode and also when the DX unit compressor is on.

input: In EnergyPlus, what happens when the DX coil is off regarding economizer operation?
output: When the DX coil is off, the economizer must meet the entire cooling load and isn’t allowed to operate in conjunction with the DX cooling coil.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is required for the Economizer Maximum Limit Dry-Bulb Temperature field?
output: The Economizer Maximum Limit Dry-Bulb Temperature field is required if Economizer Control Type 'FixedDryBulb' or 'FixedDewPointAndDryBulb' has been specified.

input: From EnergyPlus, what occurs if the outdoor air temperature exceeds the Economizer Maximum Limit Dry-Bulb Temperature?
output: If the outdoor air temperature is above the Economizer Maximum Limit Dry-Bulb Temperature, the outdoor airflow rate will be set to the minimum.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Economizer Maximum Limit Enthalpy field?
output: The Economizer Maximum Limit Enthalpy field specifies the outdoor air upper enthalpy limit for economizer operation.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if the outdoor air enthalpy exceeds the Economizer Maximum Limit Enthalpy?
output: If the outdoor air enthalpy is above the Economizer Maximum Limit Enthalpy, the outdoor air flow rate will be set to the minimum, and heat recovery will be enabled if available.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the requirement for the Economizer Maximum Limit Dewpoint Temperature field?
output: The Economizer Maximum Limit Dewpoint Temperature field is required if the Economizer Control Type 'FixedDewPointAndDryBulb' has been specified.

input: In EnergyPlus, what occurs if the outdoor air dewpoint temperature exceeds the Economizer Maximum Limit Dewpoint Temperature?
output: If the outdoor air dewpoint temperature is above the Economizer Maximum Limit Dewpoint Temperature, the outdoor airflow rate will be set to the minimum.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the Economizer Minimum Limit Dry-Bulb Temperature field specify?
output: The Economizer Minimum Limit Dry-Bulb Temperature field specifies the outdoor air temperature low limit for economizer operation.

input: From EnergyPlus, what happens if the outdoor air temperature falls below the Economizer Minimum Limit Dry-Bulb Temperature?
output: If the outdoor air temperature is below the Economizer Minimum Limit Dry-Bulb Temperature, the outdoor air flow rate will be set to the minimum, and heat recovery will be enabled if available.

input: In EnergyPlus, what should be done if no supply plenum is to be modeled?
output: Set the Supply Plenum Name to blank if no supply plenum is to be modeled.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how must a supply plenum be modeled if it is included?
output: If a supply plenum is modeled, it must be modeled as a zone with surfaces.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the supply plenum in relation to zones?
output: This supply plenum serves all zones on this system.

input: From EnergyPlus, what happens to the outlet from the system supply plenum if any zone supply plenums have been specified?
output: The outlet from the system supply plenum will flow through the zone supply plenum to the zone terminal unit.

input: In EnergyPlus, what should be done if no return plenum is to be modeled?
output: Set the Return Plenum Name to blank if no return plenum is to be modeled.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how must a return plenum be modeled if it is included?
output: If a return plenum is modeled, it must be modeled as a zone with surfaces.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the function of the return plenum in relation to zones?
output: This return plenum serves all zones on this system.

input: From EnergyPlus, what occurs to the return air from the zone if any zone return plenums have been specified?
output: The return air from the zone will flow through the zone return plenum and then into the system return plenum.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the available choices for the supply fan part-load power consumption coefficients?
output: The available choices for the supply fan part-load power consumption coefficients are InletVaneDampers, OutletDampers, VariableSpeedMotor, ASHRAE90.1-2004Appendix G, and VariableSpeedMotorPressureReset.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the supply fan part-load power coefficients?
output: The default setting for the supply fan part-load power coefficients is InletVaneDampers.

input: From EnergyPlus, where can the ASHRAE 90.1-2004 Appendix G coefficients be found?
output: The ASHRAE 90.1-2004 Appendix G coefficients can be found in TABLE G3.1.3.15, Method 2.

input: In EnergyPlus, which document provides the coefficient values for the other sets of supply fan part-load power coefficients?
output: The coefficient values for the other sets of supply fan part-load power coefficients are provided in the EnergyPlus Input Output Reference, Fan Coefficient Values table.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the basis for the VariableSpeedMotorPressureReset option?
output: The VariableSpeedMotorPressureReset option is based on Good Static Pressure Reset VSD Fan from Energy Design Resources’: Design Guidelines: Advanced Variable Air Volume (VAV) Systems.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the StayOff option indicate for Night Cycle Control?
output: StayOff means the system will remain off, no matter how hot or cold the zones may be.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens when the CycleOnAny option is selected for Night Cycle Control?
output: CycleOnAny means that if any zone served by this system has an air temperature outside the cooling or heating set points, the central fan will turn on even though the System Availability Schedule indicates the fan is off.

input: From EnergyPlus, how does the CycleOnControlZone option differ from CycleOnAny in Night Cycle Control?
output: CycleOnControlZone means the availability manager looks at the temperature in only the zone specified in Night Cycle Control Zone Name, while CycleOnAny considers temperatures in all zones served by the system.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the function of the CycleOnAnyZoneFansOnly option in Night Cycle Control?
output: CycleOnAnyZoneFansOnly is the same as CycleOnAny except that only the zone fans are cycled on and the central air handler fan is left off, applicable only if using HVACTemplate:Zone:VAV:FanPowered in one or more zones.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for Night Cycle Control?
output: The default is StayOff.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is required in the Night Cycle Control Zone Name field?
output: For the Night Cycle Control option Cycle On Control Zone, the name of the control zone must be entered; for other Night Cycle Control options, this field is ignored.

input: From EnergyPlus, what types of heat recovery can be specified in the Heat Recovery Type field?
output: The choices for Heat Recovery Type are None, Sensible, and Enthalpy.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Heat Recovery Type?
output: The default is None.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the valid range for Sensible Heat Recovery Effectiveness?
output: The valid range for Sensible Heat Recovery Effectiveness is from 0.0 to 1.0.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default value for Sensible Heat Recovery Effectiveness?
output: The default is 0.70.

input: From EnergyPlus, when is the Latent Heat Recovery Effectiveness field applicable?
output: The Latent Heat Recovery Effectiveness field is applicable if Heat Recovery Type is Enthalpy.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the valid range for Latent Heat Recovery Effectiveness?
output: The valid range for Latent Heat Recovery Effectiveness is from 0.0 to 1.0.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default value for Latent Heat Recovery Effectiveness?
output: The default is 0.65.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type field control?
output: The Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type field controls the type of automatic reset for the cooling supply air temperature.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens when the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type is set to 'None'?
output: When set to 'None', there is no reset, and the Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule or Cooling Coil Design Setpoint is used.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the 'Warmest' reset type do for the cooling supply air temperature?
output: The 'Warmest' reset type resets the cooling supply air temperature to the highest supply air temperature that will meet the cooling requirements of all zones at the maximum supply air flow rate, with a minimum setpoint of the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint and a maximum setpoint defaulted to the greater of 18C or the Heating Coil Design Setpoint plus 1.0C.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the conditions for the OutdoorAirTemperatureReset type for setting the cooling supply air temperature?
output: For the OutdoorAirTemperatureReset type, when the outdoor dry-bulb temperature (ODB) is at or below 15.6C, the setpoint is the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint plus 5.2C; when the ODB is at or above 26.7C, the setpoint is the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint; and in between, the setpoint varies linearly.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does the 'WarmestTemperatureFirst' reset type determine the cooling supply air temperature?
output: The 'WarmestTemperatureFirst' reset type finds the highest setpoint temperature that satisfies all zone cooling loads at minimum supply air flow rate; if this temperature is less than the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint, it is set to the minimum, and the supply air flow rate is increased to meet the loads.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the maximum setpoint allowed when using the 'Warmest' reset type?
output: The maximum setpoint allowed when using the 'Warmest' reset type is defaulted to the greater of 18C or the Heating Coil Design Setpoint plus 1.0C.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type?
output: The default setting for the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type is 'None'.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the available options for the Heating Coil Setpoint Reset Type?
output: The available options for the Heating Coil Setpoint Reset Type are None and OutdoorAirTemperatureReset.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens to the heating supply air temperature when the Outdoor Dry-Bulb temperature is at or below -6.7C?
output: When the Outdoor Dry-Bulb temperature is at or below -6.7C, the setpoint is the Heating Coil Design Setpoint.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Heating Coil Setpoint Reset Type?
output: The default setting for the Heating Coil Setpoint Reset Type is None.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the two dehumidification control type options available?
output: The two dehumidification control type options available are None and CoolReheat.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the CoolReheat dehumidification control type do?
output: The CoolReheat option cools beyond the dry-bulb setpoint as required to meet the humidity setpoint, with reheat provided by the terminal unit reheat coils if available.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the dehumidification control type?
output: The default setting for the dehumidification control type is None.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Dehumidification Control Zone Name field specify?
output: The Dehumidification Control Zone Name field specifies the zone name where the humidistat is located for controlling dehumidification.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Dehumidification Setpoint?
output: The default value for the Dehumidification Setpoint is 60%.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the two humidifier type options available?
output: The two humidifier type options available are None and ElectricSteam.

input: From EnergyPlus, what does the ElectricSteam humidifier option use?
output: The ElectricSteam humidifier option uses the Humidifier:Steam:Electric object.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what happens if the Humidifier Availability Schedule Name field is left blank?
output: If the Humidifier Availability Schedule Name field is left blank, the humidifier will be available anytime the system is operating.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does a schedule value of 1.0 indicate for the humidifier?
output: A schedule value of 1.0 indicates that the humidifier can be on during a given time period.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default rated moisture output rate for the humidifier?
output: The default rated moisture output rate for the humidifier is 0.000001 m3/s.

input: From EnergyPlus, how is the humidifier rated electric power determined when it is autosized?
output: When the humidifier rated electric power is autosized, it is calculated from the rated capacity in kg/s and the enthalpy rise in J/kg of the feed water from a reference temperature of liquid water at 20°C to saturated steam at 100°C.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Humidifier Control Zone Name field specify?
output: The Humidifier Control Zone Name field specifies the zone name where the humidistat is located for controlling humidification.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Humidifier Setpoint?
output: The default value for the Humidifier Setpoint is 30%.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Field: Sizing Option specify?
output: The Field: Sizing Option specifies the sizing method for the system supply air flow rate.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what are the two sizing methods available for the system supply air flow rate?
output: The two sizing methods available are Coincident sizes on the sum of the coincident zone supply air flow rates and NonCoincident sizes on the sum of the noncoincident zone design supply air flow rates.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Field: Sizing Option?
output: The default setting for the Field: Sizing Option is NonCoincident.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how should one respond to the Field: Return Fan if the system has a return fan?
output: Enter Yes if the system has a return fan.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default response for the Field: Return Fan?
output: The default response for the Field: Return Fan is No.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the Field: Return Fan Total Efficiency represent?
output: The Field: Return Fan Total Efficiency represents the ratio of the power delivered to the air to the electrical input power at maximum flow.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is the Return Fan Total Efficiency calculated?
output: The Return Fan Total Efficiency is the product of the fan motor efficiency and fan (impeller) efficiency.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the definition of motor efficiency in the context of Return Fan Total Efficiency?
output: Motor efficiency is defined as the power delivered to the shaft divided by the electrical power input to the motor.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is fan efficiency defined?
output: Fan efficiency is defined as the power delivered to the air divided by the shaft power.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the power delivered to the fluid calculated?
output: The power delivered to the fluid is calculated as the mass flow rate of the air multiplied by the pressure rise divided by the air density.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the constraints on the Return Fan Total Efficiency value?
output: The Return Fan Total Efficiency must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 1.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the Field: Return Fan Delta Pressure specify?

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Supply Fan Total Efficiency field represent?

output: The Supply Fan Total Efficiency is the product of the motor efficiency and the impeller efficiency.

output: Motor efficiency is defined as the power delivered to the shaft divided by the electrical power input to the motor.

input: In EnergyPlus, how is impeller efficiency defined?
output: Impeller efficiency is defined as the power delivered to the fluid (air) divided by the shaft power.

input: According to EnergyPlus, how is the power delivered to the fluid calculated?
output: The power delivered to the fluid is calculated as the mass flow rate of the air multiplied by the pressure rise divided by the air density.

output: The Supply Fan Motor in Air Stream Fraction field indicates the fraction of the motor heat that is added to the air stream.

output: A value of 0 means that the motor is completely outside the air stream.

output: The acceptable range for the Supply Fan Motor in Air Stream Fraction is between 0 and 1.

output: The Supply Fan Placement field specifies the supply fan placement type, which can be either DrawThrough or BlowThrough.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does DrawThrough model in terms of supply air fan placement?
output: DrawThrough models a system where the supply air fan is after the cooling and heating coils.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does BlowThrough model in terms of supply air fan placement?
output: BlowThrough models a system where the supply air fan is before the cooling and heating coils.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default setting for the Supply Fan Placement field?
output: The default setting for the Supply Fan Placement field is DrawThrough.

input: From EnergyPlus, what types of cooling coils are available?
output: The available cooling coil types are ChilledWater, ChilledWaterDetailedFlatModel, HeatExchangerAssistedChilledWater, and None.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the preferred coil model for most applications?
output: The preferred coil model for most applications is ChilledWater, which uses the COIL:Cooling:Water object with the DetailedAnalysis option.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the ChilledWaterDetailedFlatModel use?
output: ChilledWaterDetailedFlatModel uses the Coil:Cooling:Water:DetailedGeometry object.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the HeatExchangerAssistedChilledWater coil type use?
output: The HeatExchangerAssistedChilledWater coil type uses the CoilSystem:Cooling:Water:HeatExchangerAssisted, HeatExchanger:AirToAir:SensibleAndLatent, and Coil:Cooling:Water objects.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default cooling coil type?
output: The default cooling coil type is ChilledWater.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the Cooling Coil Availability Schedule Name field determine?
output: The Cooling Coil Availability Schedule Name field determines when the cooling coil is available, often used when cooling is only available seasonally.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does a schedule value of 1 indicate for the Cooling Coil Availability Schedule?
output: A schedule value of 1 indicates that the cooling coil can be on during a given time period.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does a schedule value of 0 denote for the Cooling Coil Availability Schedule?
output: A schedule value of 0 denotes that the cooling coil cannot be used during that time period.

input: In EnergyPlus, what are the options available for the Cooling Coil Setpoint Control Type?
output: The options available for the Cooling Coil Setpoint Control Type are FixedSetpoint, Scheduled, OutdoorAirTemperatureReset, Warmest, and ControlZone.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what does the FixedSetpoint control type use as the supply air setpoint?
output: The FixedSetpoint control type uses the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint as the supply air setpoint.

input: From EnergyPlus, how does the OutdoorAirTemperatureReset control type determine the supply air setpoint?
output: The OutdoorAirTemperatureReset control type varies the supply air setpoint based on values entered for Cooling Coil Setpoint at Outdoor Dry-Bulb Low, Cooling Coil Reset Outdoor Dry-Bulb Low, Cooling Coil Setpoint at Outdoor Dry-Bulb High, and Cooling Coil Reset Outdoor Dry-Bulb High.

input: In EnergyPlus, what does the Warmest control type do regarding the cooling supply air temperature?
output: The Warmest control type resets the cooling supply air temperature to the highest supply air temperature that will meet the cooling requirements of all the zones, with a minimum setpoint allowed of the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the maximum setpoint allowed for the Warmest control type?
output: The maximum setpoint allowed for the Warmest control type is defaulted to the greater of 18C or the Heating Coil Design Setpoint plus 1.0C.

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the ControlZone control type?
output: The ControlZone control type controls the supply air temperature to meet the current cooling load for the zone specified as the Cooling Coil Control Zone Name.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the default cooling coil setpoint control type?
output: The default cooling coil setpoint control type is FixedSetpoint.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what should users ensure regarding the cooling coil and heating coil setpoints?
output: Users must ensure that the cooling coil and heating coil setpoints do not overlap to avoid unwanted simultaneous heating and cooling.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the minimum cooling setpoint recommended in relation to the heating coil setpoint?
output: The cooling setpoint is recommended to always be at least 0.1C higher than the heating coil setpoint.

input: From EnergyPlus, what should be entered for the Cooling Coil Control Zone Name if the control type is ControlZone?
output: If the Cooling Coil Setpoint Control Type is ControlZone, the name of the HVACTemplate:Zone:ConstantVolume object that contains the cooling thermostat should be entered.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default value for the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint Temperature?
output: The default value for the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint Temperature is 12.8C.

input: In EnergyPlus, when is the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint Temperature used as a constant cooling supply air setpoint?
output: The Cooling Coil Design Setpoint Temperature is used as a constant cooling supply air setpoint temperature if no Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule or Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type is specified.

input: In EnergyPlus, what should be done if a constant setpoint for the cooling coil is to be specified?
output: Leave the Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule Name field blank, and the Cooling Coil Design Setpoint value will be used at all times.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule Name field?
output: It specifies the schedule name for controlling the supply air temperature delivered to the zones.

input: In EnergyPlus, how does the fan placement affect the leaving air temperature from the cooling coil?
output: For Blow Through fan placement, it is the leaving air temperature from the cooling coil, and for Draw Through fan placement, it is the leaving air temperature after the supply fan.

input: From EnergyPlus, what are the units for the values in the cooling coil setpoint schedule?
output: The values in the schedule are in degrees Celsius.

input: In EnergyPlus, when is the Cooling Coil Setpoint Schedule Name field ignored?
output: It is ignored if the Cooling Coil Setpoint Reset Type is something other than None.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default cooling coil supply air setpoint temperature when the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or below the low limit?

output: The setpoint is the value of Cooling Coil Setpoint at Outdoor Dry-Bulb Low.

output: The default is 12.8 degrees Celsius.

output: It indicates the high limit of outdoor dry-bulb temperature in degrees Celsius for outdoor air reset control.

input: From EnergyPlus, when is the Cooling Coil Setpoint at Outdoor Dry-Bulb High used?
output: It is used only when the Cooling Coil Setpoint Control Type is set to OutdoorAirTemperatureReset.

input: In EnergyPlus, what occurs when the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or above the Cooling Coil Reset Outdoor Dry-Bulb High?
output: The setpoint is the value of Cooling Coil Setpoint at Outdoor Dry-Bulb High.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default value for Cooling Coil Reset Outdoor Dry-Bulb High?
output: The default is 23.3 degrees Celsius.

input: In EnergyPlus, where is the heating coil located in relation to the cooling coil?
output: The heating coil is located in the supply air stream, upstream of the cooling coil and after the outdoor air mixing box.

input: According to EnergyPlus, what should be specified if no central heating coil is used in the Constant Volume system?

input: In EnergyPlus, what must be coordinated if a heating coil is specified?

input: From EnergyPlus, is it likely to use both a heating coil and a preheat coil at the same time?

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the purpose of the ControlZone setpoint control type?
output: The ControlZone setpoint control type controls the supply air temperature to meet the current heating load for the zone specified as the Heating Coil Control Zone Name.

input: In EnergyPlus, what is the maximum and minimum setpoint allowed when using the ControlZone control type?

input: From EnergyPlus, what is the default heating coil setpoint control type?

input: According to EnergyPlus, what should users ensure regarding the cooling coil and heating coil setpoints?

input: In EnergyPlus, how does the fan placement affect the leaving air temperature from the heating coil?
output: For Blow Through fan placement, it is the leaving air temperature from the heating coil, while for Draw Through fan placement, it is the leaving air temperature after the supply fan.

input: From EnergyPlus, what units are the values in the schedule for the heating coil setpoint temperature?
output: The values in the schedule are in degrees Celsius.

input: In EnergyPlus, when is the Heating Coil Setpoint Schedule Name field ignored?

input: According to EnergyPlus, what is the default heating coil supply air setpoint temperature when the outdoor dry-bulb temperature is at or below the low limit?
